summary: Lycoming County steel I-S tower, built 1933 and removed 1975 per the register; a 1916 newspaper item already describes a lookout tower at Waterville.

facts.status_note: The register says the steel tower was removed in 1975. No source we read describes what, if anything, remains on the site.

events.note: Department of Forestry report, 1912-13, describes an observatory on private land two miles from Waterville; not confirmed as the same site
A watcher was stationed day and night on the high lookout tower at Waterville (Wellsboro Agitator, December 13, 1916)
Watcher aided in locating fires by the smoke; a telephone linked the tower with rangers' homes
Register gives 1933 for the steel I-S tower
Register gives 1975 as the removal year
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register dates the steel I-S tower to 1933, but the 1916 Wellsboro Agitator item describes a high lookout tower at Waterville already in use. The sources do not say whether the 1933 tower replaced it or stood on the same spot. Left unresolved in the story.

notes_for_editor: Register dates (1933 build, 1975 removal) are not confirmed by any other source read. The Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1912-13 Department of Forestry report (observatory on private land two miles away, site not stated) and a December 1916 Wellsboro Agitator item (high lookout tower, watcher). The 1916 mention predates the register's build date, which is an unresolved disagreement. The firelookout.org Pennsylvania list returned 404 for both fetch and WebFetch, so the statewide inventory was not checked. The Wikipedia list of fire lookout towers has no Pennsylvania entry for these names. A Pennsylvania Forests fire-tower article mentioned in a search snippet was not read. Two WebSearch calls returned nothing Waterville-specific beyond the TopoQuest label and general background. No access or visit facts recorded: no source states them.
